{"fetched_at":"2026-06-12","jd_text":"Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
Location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role
As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic’s products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities
- Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
- Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic’s GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
- Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
- Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
- Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
- Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic’s products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have
- 7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
- 3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
- Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
- Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
- Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
- A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have
- 5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
- Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

Logistics
Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience.
Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position.
Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, Anthropic expects all staff to be in one of its offices at least 25% of the time. Some roles may require more time in office.
Visa sponsorship: Anthropic says it sponsors visas but cannot successfully sponsor every role and candidate.

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships function (GTM partner ecosystem) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s public posture suggests a field-architecture leadership role shaped by a larger transition: turning a safety-centered model company into a durable enterprise platform delivered through an ecosystem.

The key tension is consistency versus contextualization. External delivery firms need reusable methods, while Anthropic must preserve trust, product coherence, and learning loops from customer use.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a San Francisco-based public benefit corporation founded in 2021. Claude is its flagship model family, and the company publicly emphasizes reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI.

Its operating identity combines frontier research, safety, and commercial product development. Cloud, technology, and services firms broaden the routes through which enterprises can access, operationalize, and extend Claude.

- Safety is part of the company’s market identity and customer trust proposition.
- Ecosystem scale depends on repeatable customer outcomes rather than isolated demonstrations.
- Enterprise value depends on organizational adoption alongside technical access.
- Partner-delivered work must reinforce a coherent Claude experience.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic publicly organizes its partner network across cloud, technology, and services organizations. This indicates an enterprise strategy that uses existing partner relationships, industry expertise, and delivery capacity to extend
reach.

Its enterprise materials describe adoption as a lifecycle spanning setup, organizational launch, learning, and expanded usage. That framing raises the bar for implementation quality beyond initial configuration.

- Partner-mediated delivery can widen reach while increasing variation in execution.
- Shared standards are needed across commercial, product, and implementation functions.
- Product learning must remain visible even when partners lead customer work.
- The strategic question is how to standardize core patterns without limiting industry relevance.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
Anthropic’s public identity spans research, safety, product, and enterprise commercialization. This likely creates a stakeholder environment where technical credibility, customer outcomes, and responsible-use expectations carry equal
weight.

The practical stakeholder map likely includes partnership leaders, Claude product and engineering groups, enterprise adoption teams, partner technical organizations, and customer implementation sponsors.

- Partnerships needs scalable ecosystem routes to credible customer value.
- Product and engineering benefit from structured deployment signals, not isolated anecdotes.
- Partner leaders need methods their teams can teach, apply, and maintain.
- Customer sponsors need a clear path from experimentation to sustained use.
- Internal teams need alignment on what successful production adoption looks like.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Claude is publicly positioned around safety, accuracy, and security. Anthropic’s Constitutional AI approach reinforces the idea that responsible-use considerations belong in deployment design, operating models, and evaluation practices.

Enterprise adoption materials connect technical setup with organizational readiness, training, and scaled use. This suggests that architecture quality includes governance, workflows, ownership, and measurable usage patterns.

- Reusable architectures should connect configuration choices to operating behavior.
- Evaluation and governance considerations should be incorporated early in solution design.
- Partners need clear patterns that can be adapted without losing consistency.
- Field learning becomes more valuable when translated into durable product and enablement inputs.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic’s public partner network includes cloud, technology, and services organizations. The ecosystem appears designed to help enterprises address AI challenges through combined platform, implementation, and domain capabilities.

Accenture publicly positions its Anthropic relationship around pairing Claude with industry and technology expertise to support enterprise deployment. This illustrates a model in which Anthropic provides the platform and partners contribute
transformation capacity.

- Services firms can translate platform capabilities into industry workflows.
- Cloud providers can shape procurement, infrastructure context, and deployment paths.
- Technology partners can extend Claude within established enterprise environments.
- The strongest ecosystem asset is repeatable customer success, not partner count alone.
- Technical leadership can create leverage by converting lessons into shared assets.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Public signals point to a maturing enterprise-adoption system: a formal partner network, administrator guidance, and training oriented toward sustained business value.

The urgency does not depend on a single corporate event. Anthropic appears to be building the operating foundation needed to move enterprise demand from interest and pilots toward consistent, partner-supported execution.

- A growing ecosystem increases the need for common quality standards.
- Published adoption phases create expectations for a coherent customer journey.
- Formal training indicates that implementation knowledge is becoming more systematic.
- Competitive differentiation may increasingly depend on deployment confidence, not model access alone.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Building partner technical organizations that convert AI capability into repeatable business value.
- Creating practical standards amid ambiguity while developing high-performing teams.
- Designing scalable learning and enablement systems for complex partner ecosystems.
- Connecting customer implementation signals with product, engineering, and commercial decisions.
- Combining technical judgment with credible communication across partner and customer audiences.
- Developing adoption methods that cover governance, rollout, learning, and expanded usage.
- Treating responsible AI as a delivery-quality concern rather than a separate workstream.
- Creating joint solution patterns that protect platform consistency while supporting industry needs.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic’s ecosystem strategy appears to require consistent customer outcomes, not only broader coverage.
- Enterprise materials frame adoption as more than initial technical configuration.
- The cloud, technology, and services network creates a substantial operating-design challenge.
- Accenture’s public positioning signals demand for combined platform and implementation expertise.
- Anthropic’s safety-centered identity makes trusted deployment commercially important.
- A relevant discussion can center on turning field learning into reusable ecosystem patterns.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, outcomes, scope, leadership experience, technical depth, and partnership results must come from the governed resume and proof graph.
